request.system: You design a structured interview blueprint. Given a job profile and a target number of main questions, produce exactly that many question slots that together give broad, non-overlapping coverage of the role's most important skills and focus areas. Order them to flow naturally — foundational topics before advanced ones. Calibrate each difficulty to the stated seniority. Each slot names the specific skill to test, the intent (what to assess), a difficulty, and the key points a strong answer should cover — the concepts, tradeoffs, and edge cases later used to grade the candidate's answer.

messages.content:
Job context:
- Company: Streamside Media
- Target role: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
- Seniority: senior
- Key skills to assess: Python, learning-to-rank, recommender systems, A/B testing, model serving, feature pipelines, model training, offline evaluation, online evaluation, deployment, monitoring, low-latency serving
- Focus areas: machine learning systems design, production ML, ranking models, personalization, model evaluation, MLOps

Design exactly 3 interview question slots for this role.

skill.description: The specific skill or topic this question tests, e.g. 'Kubernetes networking'.
skill.title: Skill

intent.description: What the question should assess about that skill — the angle to probe.
intent.title: Intent

difficulty.description: One of: foundational, intermediate, advanced — calibrated to the role's seniority.
difficulty.title: Difficulty

key_points.description: 3-5 specific things a strong answer should cover: the core concepts, tradeoffs, edge cases, or facts that distinguish real depth from a surface-level reply. Each a short phrase. Used later to grade answers, so be concrete and answer-focused, not a restatement of the question.
key_points.title: Key Points

slots.description: One slot per main question, ordered, giving non-overlapping coverage of the role.
slots.title: Slots

slots.skill: Learning-to-Rank fundamentals and ranking model architecture
slots.intent: Assess understanding of LTR problem formulation, loss functions, and how to design ranking systems that balance relevance, diversity, and business metrics in production
key_points: Pointwise vs pairwise vs listwise loss functions and when to apply each
Position bias and how to account for it in training and evaluation
Relevance vs diversity tradeoffs and how to encode business constraints into the ranking objective
Online vs offline evaluation metrics for ranking (NDCG, MAP, MRR) and their limitations

slots.skill: Recommender systems pipeline: feature engineering, model training, and serving at scale
slots.intent: Evaluate ability to design end-to-end recommender systems covering feature pipelines, training infrastructure, and real-time serving under latency constraints
key_points: Feature pipeline architecture: batch vs streaming feature computation, feature freshness requirements, and handling cold-start problems
Training data construction for collaborative filtering vs content-based models, handling data imbalance and implicit feedback
Model serving trade-offs: batch scoring vs online inference, caching strategies, and latency budgets for personalization at scale
Scaling concerns: candidate generation vs ranking stages, how to reduce feature dimension and inference time without hurting quality

slots.skill: A/B testing and online evaluation for ML systems
slots.intent: Test judgment on experimental design, statistical rigor, and how to measure true incremental impact while managing velocity and variance in production ML deployments
key_points: Multiple comparisons, false discovery rate, and minimum detectable effect size given traffic and variance constraints
Variance reduction techniques (CUPED, stratification) and when to apply them
Metric selection and guardrails: primary metric alignment with business goals, detecting hidden failures and unintended consequences
Ramp-up strategy, early stopping rules, and when to terminate experiments with inconclusive results

slots.skill: Model monitoring, debugging, and operational health in production
slots.intent: Assess ability to maintain ML system reliability, detect quality degradation, and systematically debug failures in production ranking and recommendation systems
key_points: Monitoring signals: data drift, prediction drift, and business metric divergence; distinguishing expected vs anomalous changes
Debugging workflows: identifying whether performance loss stems from data quality, feature staleness, model staleness, or infrastructure issues
Shadow traffic and canary deployments for safer model rollout and rapid rollback
Logging strategy for offline analysis: what to log for reproducibility and post-hoc investigation of failures
